order.why: Rule 1: a sharp V at 15002 where a 137-cm muon meets a 31-cm proton whose dQ/dx rises monotonically along the proton template to 235000 at 15004; prongs at about 104 degrees, and 15023 is only a collinear mid-point of that proton.

Trap 3 avoided: the deg-2 vertex 5003 that reads 2-of-2-away has its prongs 167 degrees apart, while p4 shows the 104k at 5000 is only 2 cm of proton-stub contamination on a flat MIP track that Braggs at 5001, so 5000 with its 213k 3 cm proton stub is the vertex.

Rule1: at 17001 a 9.7cm proton starts with a textbook monotone Bragg (140k->290k) into 17002 at 84deg, while the 168cm track leaving it is flat MIP with no Bragg and simply exits the y=200 top wall; 17001 is also the lowest-z structure in the event.

Trap 3 avoided: the 2-of-2-away vertex 5004 has prongs 169 degrees apart, while p4 shows a 4.9 cm proton falling 258k->155k away from 5002 and the 52 cm muon Bragging to 168k at 5005 with an 11 cm Michel hanging off that far end.
Rule 1+3: a 4 cm 117256 e/cm proton stub sits at 14004 and the 97.7 cm muon rises away to 113810 at 14003, where a 15.6 cm 'e' Michel plus blobs 45019/39007 mark the stopping end; 97 degree opening.
Rule 1: degree-4 apex with a 90 cm proton rising to 195600 at 16005, a 7 cm 149-165k proton stub, a 292 cm muon and a 62 cm pion, all leaving; zoom shows a clean 4-prong junction.

Abstain. Cluster 27 is settled by rule 3 - 0 of 2 prongs rise away from 27006 and a hooked Michel-like segment hangs off that end. Cluster 21 is genuinely unreadable: the 8.4 cm prong does Bragg away from 21000 (rule-1 positive) but both it and the muon end show the same 2 cm hot patch followed by a 3 cm sub-MIP hole, which is a charge artefact rather than a monotone Bragg, so I cannot direct either prong; the remaining candidates are sub-cm blobs.

Abstain by rule 3: the 195 cm track enters at the y=200 top wall and rises monotonically along the muon template to 160k at 12003 with a 13 cm Michel hanging off that same end, so 12003 is a stopping end, and every other candidate is a sub-cm blob.

The only track in the event is flat MIP with delta spikes from 8000 and climbs a clean stopping-muon Bragg 60k->215k at 8001, so rule 1 names 8000; 8000 lies 3cm off the y=-200 bottom face and the track runs backward in z, but nothing enters upward through the floor, so 8000 is the closest candidate to the interaction point on either reading.
Rule 8 territory - just two isolated blobs; I take the cooler, lower-z end of the only fitted 18 cm segment, but the three sub-cm dots at z=200-210 are an equally arbitrary choice.

Rule7/2: compact 25cm spray whose cone apex and lowest-z point is 10001 (z=103), with the spray (10004, 10000, 10005, cluster 36) opening downstream from it; the 12.4cm 2-MIP proton-like prong leaving 10001 gets hotter toward its far end 10004.

Messy 40cm all-'e' object hugging the x=200 anode; the only genuine multi-prong branch point is 17004 (3 prongs), with a 33cm leg Bragging at 17001 and shower fragments piled at the x~200 end -- rule 1 favours 17008 but that is a collinear 168deg pair with a duplicate prong and an unphysical 13k e/cm reading (gap artifact).

Rule 1 partially: a genuine 56 degree kink where a long low-dQ/dx arm meets a hot 130k 10 cm prong, and the arm's apparent rise at the junction is only a 1.5 cm spike; the nearby cluster-50 bundle is ruled out as a competitor because its prongs at 50025 are 175 and 158 degrees apart (one straight object, trap 3), but every p4 profile here is a hot patch rather than a monotone Bragg so this is not certain.

Rule 1: seg20005 is a textbook monotone Bragg (43k->270k, proton template) stopping at deg-1 20001, so it starts at 20004; the 20004-20006-20002-20008 chain is collinear with the 228cm MIP muon that exits at z=499, so the muon starts at 20004 too, and seg20006 also rises away.

Cluster 15 is one straight 133cm particle entering at the z=0 upstream face (15001, clean end, no vertex activity) with dQ/dx rising monotonically to a textbook proton Bragg at 15000; the only hadronic-vertex-like point is 15002 where a 9.2cm Bragg-terminated prong branches off, so I name it but the incoming leg cools away from it.

Single 91 cm flat MIP track, no Bragg at either end; 22001 sits exactly on the y=+200 face so I take the free mid-volume end 22000, but its last dQ/dx point collapses to 10k, which looks like fit truncation that could be hiding a Bragg.

The whole event is one perfectly straight 25.5cm stopping proton (255k Bragg at 21000, falling along the proton template to ~120k at the other end); the 1.9cm stub is collinear at 180deg so it is the proton's own first cm, making 21015 the free end where the proton started.

Clusters 26, 19 and 67 are one continuous curved track with dQ/dx rising monotonically 27k->33k->54k->112k, so it ranges out at the 67 blob and starts at 26002; but that start is 8cm below the top face at z=6 with the track heading downward, which reads just as well as an entering cosmic with no visible neutrino at all, and 19001 is only 7cm away in the adjacent cluster.

Two Bragg ends in one cluster (295k at 8000 on the proton template, 185k with a reddening last 5cm at 8001) and 8002 is the junction they both point away from, 2/2 rising away; dropped a tier because the prongs leave 8002 at 172 degrees and 8002 sits on the cathode.

Rule 1 and rule 2 both favour 4003 only weakly - the 54.9 cm track leaves it at MIP and rises to a 215k Bragg at 4001, it has 1 prong rising away against 0 at 4002, and it is 7 cm lower in z - but the three-proton knot at 4002 is only 7.9 cm away across a 47 degree kink and is an equally good reading, so this is close to a coin flip.

Rule 1 at the four-proton knot: 7 cm proton rising away to 208k at 16008 plus a 3 cm 177k stopping stub, the one adverse segment (72 cm mu, 18k) excluded as a degree-4 junction fade at 16004; 16002 also has the tightest cone apex in p5 (0.5 cm RMS at 4 cm, far-near +2.5) and sits in dark-red charge, while 16004 sits in a hole.

The 390 cm cluster is one straight muon (the 13002 junction is 180 deg collinear) entering near the cathode/z wall and stopping with a 425k Bragg at 13001, so I take the separate 11 cm track and its cooler, lower-z end 47014.
Start of a 120cm MIP track that exits at z=501, with a 2.4cm 217k proton stub 1.4cm away; only the id among the near co-located ends is at risk.

Rule 1 plus the p4 shape: the 141 cm track rises over its last 10 cm onto the stopping-muon template at 20001, so the far end 20003 is the vertex even though it lies on the x=+200 anode; the anti-beam direction that implies is why this stays unclear.

Rule 1 leaves only 6000 (1/1 rising away, weak Bragg at 6002), but the 247 cm track runs downward and strongly backward in z from the x=-200 anode face, so this is very likely a cosmic and the neutrino is not readable.

18002 has both prongs MIP at the junction and hot far ends, but p4 shows those hot ends are 1-2 cm spikes rather than monotone Braggs, and the 18001 zoom shows this same track turning roughly 90 deg twice within 20 cm - so the kink at 18002 is not distinctive against the track's own wiggle.

In a 106-cluster mess I took the deg-4 knot that launches the 113.8 cm pi+ (stopping hot at 9000) and carries a 164k proton stub, but 9020 at 1.8 cm, shower apex 9007 and the hot star 9025 are all live alternatives.

Two long arms meet at a 117deg corner: dQ/dx measured outward from 24005 rises monotonically 46k -> 108k over 155cm to the stopping muon at 14000, while the other arm ends hot and shower-like at 24004, and one particle cannot stop at both ends. Not certain because the junction region spans 23cm across a cluster boundary.

The 175 cm muon is flat MIP with no Bragg at 21005 and runs forward to z=495, so it starts there, and the 10 cm proton attached at the same point rises 137k->205k away from it; preferred over the rival junction 28013, whose 47.5 cm proton profile is dropout-ridden and non-monotone and whose 32 cm mu is flat, and because ten small clusters sit within 40 cm of 21005 and none near 28013.

The 125 cm track's smooth monotone 140k-to-60k decay over the first 15 cm from 29008 is a real Bragg there (the spiky rise at the other end is contamination from the 4 cm 193k proton stub sitting on 29010), so the track originates at 29010, where two short hot proton stubs also start; the 395 cm cluster 22 is a separate vertical cosmic.

In a large EM shower this is the one junction of two heavily-ionising prongs, and prong 95135 is a textbook proton - 56k leaving the vertex rising to 149k Bragg at 95153 - sitting at the upstream end of the hot core.

Rule 1: the contained 222cm MIP ends in an unmistakable Bragg rise to 455k at 16001 with a small blob 11cm off it, so the start is 16000, where the first 5cm carry a 210k vertex blob; low-z rule 2 loses to this.

The 8001/65012 pair is a 175 deg break in one continuous 255 cm track, not a junction, and 8000 is a clean monotone Bragg stop, leaving 65011 as the only non-stopping free end and the lowest-z point; but its 105k tip peaks 1.5 cm in, so it could equally be a cosmic entering near the cathode.

The 185 cm cluster is an entering-stopping muon (MIP at the x=-201 face, monotone Bragg to 250k at 13002) so 13000 is the only rule-1-clean candidate, but everything else in the event is sub-centimetre.

Rule 1 on the only cleanly fitted segment in the junction: the 32cm proton rises monotonically 80k to 280k away from here and stops at 17006, and nothing rises toward this point; 17003 (2.8cm away, where the muon terminates) is the alternative, so not certain.
Very fragmented shower event; 109123 is the lowest-z deg-4 hub with 2 prongs rising away and a shower-like cone, but the 50 cm Bragg proton starts 50 cm away at 109168.

Rule 1: both heavy prongs rise away from 59038 and terminate in real Bragg ends at 59037 and 59039, and the free end of the 131 cm MIP (11004) sits 5 cm away, so this is the fitted start of the hadronic prongs.

A four-prong heavily-ionising proton star with the charge peaking at 20006 (288-395k) and prongs Bragg-stopping at 20003 and 20002, and the 67.6 cm flat-MIP track back-extrapolates to within 1.1 cm of 20006 versus 2.1 cm of 20054.

Rule 1 at the only 4-prong: three protons (48.9, 9.0, 4.4 cm) all start near MIP at 11005 and rise monotonically to 230k/230k/265k Bragg stops, while 11007 is excluded as a 158 deg through-going kink; downgraded because the surviving MIP arm runs 206 cm backward to the z=0 face.

The 98cm muon shows a clean monotone Bragg rise to 150k along the stopping-muon template at its far end 20001, so it starts at 20008, and the EM shower leaves the same junction the other way at 113 degrees; the only ambiguity is 20033 2.4cm away.

Rule 1 plus the p4 shape: the 229 cm muon has a genuine monotone Bragg to 140k at 16001, so 16000 is the cool end, but 16000 sits on the y=-200 floor and that reading needs an upward and backward-going particle, which is why I am not confident.

Rule 1 on the two informative prongs: p4 shows textbook proton Braggs at the far ends of both (255000 at 8003 and 240000 at 8011), both pointing away from 8010; the third 40 cm prong is hotter at 8010, which I am reading as vertex-charge overlap rather than a real rise, hence not certain.
Two clusters start 2.7 cm apart at z about 2: the 134 cm track (rises away x5.04) and a 12 cm proton stopping at 170k; 8001 is the muon start of that V.
Rule 1: cool 100k start of a 24cm proton with a textbook Bragg rise to 158k; the only rival is a bare track end sitting on the z+ wall.
Both prongs rise away: a 7.2cm proton Bragging at 313k and a 95.6cm muon Bragging at 155k with a Michel hanging off that far end, which rule 3 says is never the vertex.
